A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same vocabulary-scaling study. All 21 pages, including Appendices A–I, are readable, and the text, equations, tables, and figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original tokenizer measurements, language-model training experiments, downstream evaluations, and supplementary controls, including Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results, including vocabulary-scaling experiments on FineWeb-Edu and OpenWebText and the analyses in Appendices B–H.

M1.justification: The BPE procedures, model architectures, training objectives, and loss-decomposition approach remain unchanged. Revisions explain the existing approach without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training corpora, downstream benchmarks, Paloma evaluation data, and word-frequency proxy. No dataset, task, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The BPE/SuperBPE comparisons, Pythia and OLMo-2 models, parameter-matched configurations, and tied-versus-untied comparisons retain the same participants.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 and Appendix I retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, model sizes, and optimization settings. The revised justification for unigram entropy does not change its calculation.

E4.justification: The cross-corpus, parameter-matching, tied-embedding, frequency-group, and learning-rate analyses remain unchanged. Neither PDF presents a corresponding norm-constraining ablation supporting the sentence deleted from the conclusion.

E5.justification: Both versions state that every experiment was repeated with five seeds. The plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged, with no added run information or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted trends are unchanged. Section 7 deletes one qualitative outcome assertion: that norm-constraining removes vocabulary-scaling gains. This is a limited deletion of reported prose; neither PDF supplies supporting experimental details or ablation data.

T1.justification: The minimal-description-length definition, Kolmogorov-complexity bound, loss equations, and Appendix A derivation are unchanged. The new statistical-pattern explanation is interpretive prose, not a revised formal definition or proof.

C1.justification: Section 7 removes the claim that norm-constraining confirms causality and softens vocabulary growth from providing no segmentation refinement to providing minimal refinement. The abstract and central frequent-word benefit claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 and 5.1 reframe complexity reduction as reducing the statistical patterns models must learn. Section 3.2 replaces the fair-comparison rationale for unigram entropy with small-dataset stability and reduced sparsity concerns.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, architectural configurations, and the code and model-resource links remain unchanged, including Tables 8–9 and Appendix I.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged. Reusing the FineWeb citation in Section 3.3 and specifying tokenizer vocabulary size in Section 6 do not substantively alter research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the contribution paragraph, complexity explanation, discussion, and conclusion without reorganizing sections. Section 4.2 replaces Figure ?? with Figures 2 and 3, and Appendix A removes unresolved appendix references.

P2.justification: Page 4 has small equation-spacing and text-flow changes that shift Table 1 slightly. All figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and section locations; no display is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 removes the unsupported norm-constraining claim from the conclusion and repairs or removes broken cross-references, improving evidential consistency and navigation. The empirical evidence and formal mathematics remain unchanged. The revised pattern-count explanation remains informal, and the introduction retains broader causal language, so the improvement is limited.
